abstract: Abstract Virtual influencers have become an established part of influencer marketing, yet their effectiveness, the mechanisms underlying their persuasive impact, and the boundary conditions shaping these effects remain unclear. We address these questions through a meta-analysis of 210 independent experimental studies and 643 effect sizes. Virtual influencers generate greater novelty but lower credibility than human influencers, revealing a systematic trade-off between novelty- and credibility-based persuasion, with the relative importance of these mechanisms shifting over time from novelty toward credibility. Virtual influencer effectiveness further depends on anthropomorphic design and contextual congruence. Highly anthropomorphic virtual influencers benefit from artificial intelligence integration, futuristic positioning, and rational, proximal messaging, whereas low-anthropomorphism virtual influencers perform better with emotional and distal framing. Meta-analytic structural equation modeling supports a dual-pathway process in which credibility-based indirect effects are stronger for highly anthropomorphic virtual influencers, whereas novelty-based indirect effects are stronger for low-anthropomorphism virtual influencers. These results establish anthropomorphism as a structural boundary condition in influencer marketing.

ur.ai_reason: 虚拟影响者与AI相关但非核心，消费者说服机制和效果的元分析，属CX/消费者行为
ur.tldr: 通过对210项实验研究、643个效应量的元分析，揭示虚拟影响者比人类影响者具有更高新奇度但更低可信度，呈现新奇度与可信度间的系统性权衡，且该权衡随时间从新奇度向可信度迁移。拟人化是关键边界条件：高拟人化虚拟影响者受益于AI整合、未来定位和理性近端信息，低拟人化者更适合情感远端框架。研究确立拟人化为影响者营销的结构性边界条件。

title: Virtual influencer marketing: A meta-analytic review
title_zh: 虚拟网红营销：元分析综述
